title: parse_csv_line ignores quoting and breaks on embedded commas
problem:
The function `parse_csv_line(line)` in csvp.py should parse a single CSV line and return the list of fields. Quoting rules follow RFC 4180:

- Fields are separated by commas.
- A field may be enclosed in double quotes ('"'). Inside a quoted field, commas are literal (not separators).
- Inside a quoted field, a doubled double-quote ('""') is a literal '"' character.
- Whitespace around a field is preserved as part of the field (fields are NOT stripped).
- An empty line returns a single empty field: [''].
- A trailing comma creates a trailing empty field: 'a,' -> ['a', ''].
- A quoted empty field returns an empty string: '""' -> [''].
- Quotes only have syntactic meaning when they open a field (the first character of a field). Quotes appearing mid-field are treated as literal characters (this is a pragmatic choice; well-formed CSV will not do this).

The current implementation splits on ',' and ignores quoting entirely, so embedded commas and escaped quotes inside quoted fields are mishandled. Do NOT use the `csv` module — implement the parser directly. Fix the implementation so every hidden test passes.
